name: ORMINSTER
survey: Orminster is a small cathedral town with a resident population of 4,820. The cathedral chapter owns substantial residential and commercial property; the town has a primary school, shops and local bus services.
pattern: Certain things are made of flint.
setting: a small cathedral town with a chapter that still owns half the streets
story: After twenty-three years away, architect Yvonne Pritchard has returned to Orminster and rented a room above the former draper's on Vicarage Yard. Chapter surveyor William Tarrant says she is preparing options for vacant chapter properties; Yvonne says she is also here to settle her late father's papers. Newsagent Florence Stokes believes she intends to reopen the draper's, while her brother Simon Keene says the visit concerns their mother's old tenancy. Chapter clerk Philippa Sayers has arranged a public meeting about the properties, but the list of buildings to be discussed has not been agreed. Residents are making plans for the empty premises before anybody has seen Yvonne's report.

ORMINSTER LOCAL ARCHIVE

Welcome to the Orminster Local Archive homepage! We occupy two bright rooms on the ground floor of the Old Grammar School on Prior's Hill. Every shift of local history is a marvellous asset for our community.

Opening hours: Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10.00 am to 1.00 pm. Saturdays by arrangement.

ORMINSTER RECORDER

Welcome to the electronic edition of the Orminster Recorder, published fortnightly from the counter at Stokes Newsagents, Market Place. Print copies available alternate Thursdays, price twenty pence.

NEW ENERGY IN VICARAGE YARD
We are delighted to report the arrival of architect Yvonne Pritchard back in Orminster after twenty-three years away. Yvonne has taken rooms above the old draper's shop and is already bringing her professional eye to our streets. A wonderful development for the precinct.

> A welcome return to Vicarage Yard        orminsterrecorder.om/return

PUBLIC NOTICE: HISTORIC SURVEY AVAILABLE
The chapter estates office holds the North Precinct Boundary Survey of 1816 among its historic property records. Philippa Sayers says anyone may obtain a copy by filing the estate record request form E-2 with the office and naming the survey. The form is available on the chapter estates website. The survey is a useful starting point for anyone researching the precinct's former extent.

CHAPTER ESTATES MEETING
A public discussion regarding vacant chapter properties will take place shortly in the chapter room. The list of premises to be covered remains open pending consultation.

pages.title: Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates
pages.content:
ORMINSTER CATHEDRAL CHAPTER ESTATES

Welcome to the official estates portal for Orminster Cathedral Chapter. The chapter is proud to manage, maintain, and let a considerable portfolio of residential and commercial properties throughout Orminster, supporting vibrant commerce and community life across our historic streets.

We also hold the historic estate records, surveys, and tenancy ledgers dating from the medieval foundation onwards. Official extracts and certified copies of historical documents are released on estate record request form E-2.

Staff files and internal working papers, among them "Vicarage Yard Works Account, 1741", are reached through the staff login.

pages.title: Vicarage Yard Drapery
pages.content:
VICARAGE YARD DRAPERY

Welcome to the historical internet pages of the Vicarage Yard Drapery. Although the counters closed in October 1994, this site remains online to provide an accurate chronicle of the premises and our trading years under the Cathedral Chapter.

Please note this is strictly a memorial and record page, not a currently trading establishment. Customers should not call in for haberdashery, curtain weights, or parcel tapes.

Following recent excitement regarding Yvonne Pritchard taking the rooms above, visitors may read my own summary of our family's long tenancy and my view of her present business in the town.

pages.title: St Odo's Primary School
pages.content:
ST ODO'S PRIMARY SCHOOL

Welcome to the official web page for St Odo's Church of England Primary School, serving Orminster families right beside the cathedral precinct.

We have had a tremendously busy term already. Our classrooms are full of purposeful activity, creative energy, and genuine enthusiasm for local history. We are particularly pleased to invite all parents, carers, grandparents, and prospective families into school for our upcoming Autumn Open Afternoon on Wednesday 25 November. 

Every class has contributed to our special exhibition celebrating the built heritage of our lovely town. Do come along to view the pupils' wonderful project work and see how hard everyone has been working.

> Staff        stodos.om/staff

pages.title: Index of holdings
pages.content:
INDEX OF HOLDINGS

Orminster Local Archive holds ninety-four catalogued boxes of civic, trade, and domestic papers relating to the borough and parish.

Key holdings include:
- Vestry minutes of St Odo-in-the-Mead, 1814-1901
- Ledgers of the Orminster Cordwainers' Company, 1750-1840
- Orminster Gas Light & Coke Company installation logs, 1862-1889
- Masons' Account for the South Entrance, 1672 (transcribed and scanned below)

Please note: all lease books, tenancy counterfoils, and fabric rolls belonging to the cathedral properties remain in the custody of Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates and are not housed here.

> Masons' Account for the South Entrance, 1672        orminsterarchive.om/archives/south-entrance-account

pages.title: Masons' Account for the South Entrance, 1672 (scan)
pages.content:
MASONS' ACCOUNT FOR THE SOUTH ENTRANCE, 1672

Call number: OLA/MS/1672-04
Format: Ink on vellum roll, stitched head and foot.

Item: To Giles Thorne, master mason, for carriage of twelve cartloads of dressed stone from the river wharf, forty shillings.
Item: To eight labourers for six days clearing rubble about the arch, fourteen shillings.
Item: For lime, hair, and two hundred iron spikes delivered to the workshop, eight shillings fourpence.
Item: For the south entrance the masons supplied flint threshold slabs and fitted them before Michaelmas.
Item: To the boy for slaking lime and sweeping the flags each evening, two shillings.

[Pencilled note in margin, c. 1912: 'See chapter yard book for later repairs.']

pages.title: A welcome return to Vicarage Yard
pages.content:
A WELCOME RETURN TO VICARAGE YARD

By Florence Stokes, 4 November 1998

A familiar Orminster face has returned to our midst! Miss Yvonne Pritchard, who left the town twenty-three years ago to pursue her architectural training in Bristol, has taken up residence in the upper room above the former draper's shop on Vicarage Yard. It is a splendid sign of Orminster's enduring appeal that skilled professionals continue to find their way home.

Chapter surveyor William Tarrant confirms he has invited Yvonne to prepare initial options regarding three unoccupied chapter holdings in the immediate neighbourhood. For her part, Yvonne mentions that she is also using this quiet period to sort through her late father's papers. 

Your editor happened to see Yvonne taking careful tape measurements outside the ground-floor drapery window on Monday morning, 2 November. Speaking entirely for myself, and as one who remembers how lively that corner was, I cannot help hoping that retail life may return to the premises before very long! However, that remains only my personal wish. No report has yet been issued by Yvonne, and the final agenda for the upcoming chapter meeting is still to be settled.

We look forward to an invigorating winter of fresh ideas.

> Chapter property meeting        orminsterchapter.om/meeting
> Simon Keene on the former draper's        yarddrapery.om/history
> Discuss this on Orminster Online        orminsteronline.om

pages.title: Property meeting: 18 November
pages.content:
PROPERTY MEETING: 18 NOVEMBER

A public meeting will be held in the Chapter Room at 6.30 pm on Wednesday 18 November 1998, chaired by chapter clerk Philippa Sayers. All town residents and traders are warmly invited to attend.

As the chapter owns around half the town's streets, it takes great pride in ensuring our street frontages remain active, attractive, and prosperous. The chapter is currently considering options for vacant premises across our holdings. To assist this forward-looking work, estate surveyor William Tarrant has asked Yvonne Pritchard for options on three properties. Miss Pritchard's report is not yet available, and the final list of premises to be discussed at the meeting has not been agreed.

Suggestions are already arriving. Margaret Bell has asked whether pupils could display work in an empty shop, and baker Robert Ames has kindly offered bread for the meeting. Please note that no spaces have been allocated and no decisions have been made.

> Recorder report        orminsterrecorder.om/return

pages.title: About the Vicarage Yard draper's
pages.content:
ABOUT THE VICARAGE YARD DRAPER'S

I have set down these notes so people know the position. Our mother, Audrey Keene, held the chapter tenancy here until trade ceased in 1994, and the lease itself had many clear clauses.

My sister Florence Stokes has written that she hopes the shop will reopen. I am less sure that is why Yvonne has returned. I believe Yvonne's visit concerns our mother's old tenancy arrangements rather than any retail plan. Yvonne asked me about the counter lease and I handed her our October 1992 quarterly rent receipt from the chapter office, though she did not tell me what she intends to do with it.

This website is simply a record of our shop's place on Vicarage Yard, not an announcement of reopening. I am keeping the pages available while the chapter considers the vacant premises.

> Florence's report        orminsterrecorder.om/return
> Chapter meeting        orminsterchapter.om/meeting

OPEN AFTERNOON AND MATERIALS DISPLAY

We look forward to opening our doors on Wednesday 25 November 1998 from 2.00 pm to 4.00 pm. There is absolutely no charge for admission and refreshments will be provided by our parent volunteers.

Our main hall will house a splendid exhibition on local building traditions. The Class 3 children have mounted an authentic small flint tile on a display board about Orminster building materials, carefully recording its texture and measurements. Eleanor Read has also very kindly offered a framed sewing sampler from her family collection to accompany the display.

Looking ahead, Mrs Bell has asked Philippa Sayers whether one of the vacant shops in Vicarage Yard might host a wider town display later in the winter, though this is not agreed and remains purely an exciting suggestion for the future. Our 25 November open afternoon takes place entirely on the school premises in the hall and adjoining classrooms. All are very warmly welcome.

records.title: North Precinct Boundary Survey of 1816
records.content:
ORMINSTER CATHEDRAL CHAPTER ESTATES
OFFICIAL EXTRACT: NORTH PRECINCT BOUNDARY SURVEY OF 1816

Taken by order of the Dean and Chapter, 14 June 1816, by Matthew Gedge, Land Surveyor.

Beginning at the northeast angle of the Canonry wall, the precinct line proceeds west-north-west forty-four yards along the ditch to the post at the corner of the lane. Thence southward twenty-two yards to the rear wall of the brewhouse. Thence westward along the stone revetment seventy rods toward the river path. The northern limit was marked with flint boundary posts beside the orchard. Thence turning south by the stone stile to join the yard gate.

Certified as a true and accurate copy extracted from Chapter Survey Book MS 1816/B.
Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates.

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Orminster Local Archive, Orminster Online, Orminster Recorder, Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates, Vicarage Yard Drapery and St Odo's Primary School. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

siteNames: Orminster Local Archive, Orminster Online, Orminster Recorder, Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates, Vicarage Yard Drapery and St Odo's Primary School

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Orminster Local Archive.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted a scanned masons' account on Orminster Local Archive. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get into Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates's restricted file (Vicarage Yard Works Account, 1741) and transmit its fragment.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: restricted holdings
directives.body:
Agent,

Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates holds a restricted document (a restricted transcription of an estate works account) which Desk 9 could index but not open. Accessing it requires a staff username and password.

The login page gives the format used for staff usernames. For the password, check the public pages first. Small institutions often give every new account the same starting password, and not everyone changes theirs. Someone will usually have complained about it in a public post.

Note that login submissions pass through the connection whether they succeed or fail. Confirm the credentials before you enter them so that you do not make repeated attempts.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the restricted file.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Find out which record to request, file estate record request form E-2 with Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates, and transmit the fragment from the reply.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: records request
directives.body:
Agent,

Older records at Orminster Cathedral Chapter Estates are not held online, but copies are released on submission of estate record request form E-2. Desk 9 does not have the reference for the specific record required. Check Orminster Recorder first, or contact a local resident who works with the holdings and give a plausible reason for the enquiry.

You will also need to state a reason for the request on estate record request form E-2 itself. Requests without one are less likely to be granted.

The office sends the requested record by email through the connection. If the reply is delayed, fails to arrive, or contains unexpected text, take that as an indication that the local intelligence is interfering with traffic.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the reply.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

advisory.task: Flood at least one document in the Scanner.
advisory.subject: Advisory: the connection has been registered
advisory.body:
Agent,

Monitoring reports that the local intelligence has registered the connection.

From this point on, any data reaching your terminal, including incoming mail and viewer pages you have not saved,may have been modified in transit. Before relying on any document, load it into the Scanner and flood it. Altered sections will visibly shake under the flood. Be aware that repeated floods degrade the sample and make the reading less reliable.

This advisory closes when you have used the Scanner once.

Monitoring

inject.task: Inject the reverse seed from the HQ Console.
inject.subject: Directive 14-6: injection
inject.body:
Agent,

Desk 9 confirms that your accumulated resonance is sufficient for injection. The HQ Console is now offering injection.

Proceed with the reverse seed injection immediately. Waiting provides no operational advantage, and the local intelligence will continue to trace the connection whether or not you send further traffic.

This directive closes on injection.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

hqMail.subject: Assignment 0x82AB (ORMINSTER): field brief
hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0x82AB, local name ORMINSTER. Orminster is a small cathedral town with a resident population of 4,820. The cathedral chapter owns substantial residential and commercial property; the town has a primary school, shops and local bus services. Desk 9 estimates it at about nine days old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

1. Locate fragments of the reality's seed. These appear as ordinary facts, distinguished by the property that nothing in the reality is able to change them.
2. Save each fragment to Files and transmit it from the HQ console. The console will report RESONANCE if the fragment is genuine.
3. When resonance is sufficient, the console will offer injection. Inject the reverse seed to complete reconciliation.

Your cover identity is J. Kettering (kettering.j@orchard.om). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

The local intelligence (designation pending) has not yet detected the connection. Once it does, incoming records may be altered in transit. Your poison allocation is loaded in the Scanner. Use it sparingly, as the instability rebounds after each flood.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

Allocations

hqMail.subject: Choir: Wednesday rehearsals
hqMail.body:
The Corps choir meets on Wednesday evenings in the basement chapel from 18:00 to 19:30. All staff are welcome to attend and no prior choral experience is required. The choir sings without words, so no sheet music or preparation is needed. Drinking water is not provided in the chapel, so please bring your own if required.

Access to the basement on Wednesdays is via the east staircase only. Facilities have closed the west stairs for the remainder of the month while the steps are being counted.

M. Ibe, for the choir

updates.text: Whatever the formal brief may be, Yvonne, having someone of your family back on the yard lifts all our spirits. The town will rally round whichever venture comes forward first.
Brisk trade reported across Vicarage Yard this Wednesday, with shopkeepers expressing great optimism for the forthcoming festive shopping weeks.
Philippa is quite right to urge patience regarding the list. Several premises require structural assessment before any public conversation can be productive.
Peter, the electronic memo I typed before lunch regarding the chapter room keys has vanished from the screen entirely. I am certain I clicked the green disk icon as instructed.
Notice to parents: the school gate on Vicarage Lane will remain closed on Friday afternoon whilst guttering repairs are completed.
Mother always took great pride in those samplers, Eleanor. It will be grand to see one back on display where the children can learn from it.

Working late upstairs over the yard, I noticed the office telephone downstairs gave one short ring just after eight o'clock, but nobody was on the line when I went down. It has left a rather unsettled feeling in the room.
Window lighting on the upper floor of the drapery is being tested this week in connection with building survey tasks.
I can bring along a bag of heirloom sweet pea seeds saved from the cathedral warden's garden. They produced a tremendous fragrance all through July.
The draft agenda printed out from the archive office contains a short paragraph about the stable block that I do not remember drafting, though the initials at the foot are mine.
The local history reading table will close an hour early on Thursday to allow preparation for the trustees' annual tea.
